html:
The westward migration of the ancestors of the Romani people, who left northern India about a thousand years ago and reached Europe by the later Middle Ages.

Their origin was long a mystery; Europeans wrongly took them for Egyptians, which gave the word "Gypsy". Language solved it. In the 18th century scholars saw that Romani is an Indo-Aryan language, related to Sanskrit and to Hindi and Punjabi. Genetic studies later agreed: the Roma descend from a group that left northwest India, probably between the 6th and 11th centuries.

Their path can be read in loanwords. They passed through Persia, then Armenia, and lived for a long time in the Byzantine Empire, which left many Greek words in Romani. From the 14th century they are recorded across the Balkans and then all of Europe.

Life there was often hard. In Wallachia and Moldavia, Roma were held as slaves until the 1850s. Under Nazi rule hundreds of thousands were murdered in the Romani Holocaust, alongside the Holocaust of the Jews. Today Roma form Europe's largest ethnic minority.
sum: The westward migration of the ancestors of the Romani people, who left northern India about a thousand years ago and reached Europe by the later Middle Ages.
